question: Can a simple deterministic rule safely accept enough historically correct LLM/retrieval intent disagreements to clear every V112 full-policy gate while leaving the transferred abstention novelty signal unchanged?
rescueEligibility: direct typed status is KNOWN but exact proposed intent disagrees with deterministic nearest-intent retrieval

selection.feasibleCandidateDefinition: all seventeen frozen V112 quality gates pass noncompensatorily
selection.selectionObjective: prefer feasible; then maximum passed-gate count, minimum normalized violation of failed gates, minimum mean regret, minimum false-known acceptance, maximum known exact-intent accuracy, minimum complexity, lexical signature
selection.evaluationRole: historical policy design only; no transfer or protected-test claim

decisionRule.ifAtLeastOneCandidateIsFeasible: freeze one selected rescue rule for separately locked evaluation on a new disjoint population
decisionRule.ifNoCandidateIsFeasible: close this simple disagreement-rescue family and require new evidence or policy structure
